name: Sliding window + counting array
space: O(10⁴): one counter per possible value
whenToUse: The standard answer. Values are at most 10⁴, so a counting array works; with bigger values you would use a hash set instead.

card.signals: "subarray" (contiguous), "unique elements" (a rule every window must keep) and "maximum sum". If a window has a repeat, every bigger window that contains it has the repeat too, so you can grow on the right and shrink on the left. All values are positive, so growing a unique window never lowers its sum.
card.pattern: a variable-size window. Each index enters the window once (right) and leaves at most once (left), so the whole scan is O(n). A running total means the sum is never added up from scratch.
card.coreIdea: add nums[right] to count and total. Only nums[right] can be a repeat, so move left to the right until its old copy is gone, taking each dropped value off total. Then compare total with best.

invariant: After each shrink loop, the window nums[left..right] has no repeats, and total is its sum.
